headline: Approved flood proofing at 75 North Street; referred a 370 Highland Avenue car wash to design review; continued six projects to November 5.
summary: Most projects were continued to November 5 for further review, including a hotel with 16 units at 11 Summer Street and 53 affordable homes on Margin Street. Approved a flood proofing plan at 75 North Street by 8-0 with one abstention. Referred the Highland Avenue car wash plan to the Design Review Board.
decisions: Continued the 11 Summer Street hotel site plan review to November 5, 2026, 9-0.
Continued the 56 Margin Street affordable homes and shelter plan to November 5, 2026, 9-0.
Continued the 440 Highland Avenue site plan review to November 5, 2026, 9-0.
Continued the 57 Wharf Street site plan review to November 5, 2026, 8-0 with one recusal.
Approved the written decision for flood proofing at 75 North Street, 8-0 with one abstention.
Referred the car wash project at 370, 378, and 382 Highland Avenue to the Design Review Board, 9-0.
Continued the 370, 378, and 382 Highland Avenue car wash project to November 5, 2026, 9-0.
Endorsed the Approval Not Required plan for 47 Congress Street, 6-3.
Continued the Approval Not Required plan for 6 Technology Way to November 5, 2026, 9-0.
Approved the September 9, 2026 Joint Public Hearing with City Council minutes, as amended, 9-0.

City of Salem Planning Board 
Minutes October 15, 2026

Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028 
through § 2-2033. 
 
 
 
 
 
MEETING AGENDA 
A public hearing for the Salem Planning Board was held on Thursday, October 15, 2026, at 6:30 
p.m. via remote access. Public participation was possible via Zoom video and conference call. 
 
Chair Kirt Rieder calls the meeting to order at 6:31 pm 
I. ROLL CALL  
Present: Chair Kirt Rieder, Vice Chair Sarah Tarbet, Jonathan Berk, Zach Caunter, Elena 
Eimert, Tom Furey, Helen Sides, Josh Turiel, and Graham Wing (9) 
Absent: (0) 
Arriving Late: (0) 
Leaving Early: (0) 
Also in attendance: Claudia Cunningham, Planner 
 
II. REGULAR AGENDA 
 
A. 11 Summer Street (Map 26, Lot 459), 5-9 Summer Street (Map 26, Lot 461), and 15 
Summer Street (Map 26, Lot 462)  
Applicant: West House LLC, Emmerton House LLC, and Peabody House LLC. 
Description: A continuance of a public hearing for all persons interested in the 
application of West House LLC, Emmerton House LLC, and Peabody House LLC, all 
d/b/a The Salem Inn, located at 5,7,9 Summer Street (Map 26, Lot 459), 11-13 
Summer Street (Map 26, Lot 461), and 15 Summer Street (Map 26, Lot 462) in the B5 
– Central Development district and Urban Renewal Overlay for Site Plan Review in 
accordance with Section 9.5 of the Salem Zoning Ordinance. Specifically, the 
applicant proposes the renovation of the existing 3 story building at 11 Summer 
Street to accommodate a hotel with 16 units. The applicant is proposing site 
renovations including an increase of parking, through exterior parking changes, and 
renovations of the existing 2 story garage. Other site improvements include 
landscape improvements, and solar car ports. 
 
*This applicant has requested to continue to November 5, 2026* 
 
Attorney Scott Grover is in attendance for the applicant and to request a 
continuance to allow for the civil engineering peer review to progress. 
 
CITY OF SALEM

through § 2-2033.

B. 56 Margin Street, 54 Margin Street, 7 High Street, 20 Endicott Street (Map 25, Lot 
597), 24 Endicott Street (Map 25, Lot 595)  
Applicant: Harborlight Homes and Lifebridge North Shore  
Description: A continuation of a public hearing for all persons interested in the 
application of Harborlight Homes and Lifebridge North Shore at 56, 54 Margin 
Street, 20 Endicott Street, 7 High Street (Map 25, Lot 597) and 24 Endicott Street 
(Map 25, Lot 595) in the Residential Two-Family District (R2), Coastal Resilience 
Overlay District (C-ROD), Flood Hazard Overlay District (FHOD), and Smart Growth 
Overlay District (SGOD) for Smart Growth Overlay Plan Review and Coastal 
Resilience Overlay Site Plan Review in accordance with the following sections of the 
Salem Zoning Ordinance: Section 7.4 Smart Growth Overlay District and Section 8.9 
Coastal Resiliency Overlay District. Specifically, the applicant proposes the 
demolition of the buildings at 24 Endicott Street (Map 25, Lot 595) and 56 Margin 
Street (Map 25, Lot 597), the adaptive reuse of 54 Margin Street (Map 25, Lot 597), 
and the preservation of the façade of 20 Endicott Street (Map 25, Lot 597) to 
accommodate for a 22,806 square foot building comprised of 53 affordable homes, a 
shelter with 70 beds, and supportive programing space along with other site 
improvements. Thirteen parking spaces are proposed on site. 
*This item was heard 4th* 
Mr. Rieder steps away at 6:38 to reboot his computer  
Pat Connolly, Harborlight Homes, Stefano Basso, SV Design, and Julie 
Riemenschneider, landscape architect, are in attendance for the applicant.
City of Salem Planning Board 
Minutes October 15, 2026 
Page 3 of 15 
 
Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028 
through § 2-2033. 
Ms. Cunningham says that she has received the draft of the peer review and it needs 
to be reviewed by Engineering. The peer reviewer is discussing with Engineering on 
the best course of action. Ms. Cunningham will update Mr. Connolly on October 16. 
Mr. Connolly asks if there is an example of an affordable restriction document that 
the team could use or should they use the Mass Housing document? Ms. 
Cunningham will follow up with Mr. Connolly regarding this.   
The applicant will be with the Design Review Board (DRB) on October 28, 2026. Mr. 
Basso says they will be dropping materials samples by the Planning Department  
next week.  
Mr. Rieder rejoins meeting at 6:42 
Ms. Riemenschneider shares her screen. There will be a concrete sidewalk with brick 
permeable pavers and a line of street trees along margin street, upgrading the 
streetscape. They will try to save existing trees and just add infill. This should allow 
the project to end up with a canopy over the sidewalk. There are open areas, i.e., 
entrances and outdoor areas, where they tried to use tall evergreens (emerald 
arborvitae). There is a long planter along building on Margin Street and ornamental 
grasses, evergreen shrubs and perennials. On the back of the building – added trees. 
It is very shady so the shade tolerant trees in the back. Karpick maples and American 
hornbeam. Patio areas will have black steel fencing surround.  
Public Comment 
Polly Wilbert 
7 Cedar Street 
Asks about the opportunity for residents to do gardening on the site. Ms. 
Riemenschneider says it is limited on the site but there is a possibility for the areas 
where there are proposed plantings, but the site is shady and difficult.  
Planning Board Comments 
Mr. Furey asks what the purpose of the canopy is? It may invite those to hang out. 
Ms. Riemenschneider says that it is the tree canopy that provides separation 
between the sidewalk and the traffic.  
Ms. Tarbet asks if the rear is all gravel and questions how much open space is there? 
And is the gravel space counted towards the open spaces? Could they be made 
greener and more usable? The team doesn’t know the percentage is gravel, but the 
site is shady and maintenance could be difficult. Ms. Riemenschneider says there is a 
large existing retaining wall for the playground, and space is limited in the rear. They
City of Salem Planning Board 
Minutes October 15, 2026 
Page 4 of 15 
 
Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028 
through § 2-2033. 
were thinking of low maintenance ground cover to avoid invasive plants or have the 
areas overgrown. Mr. Rieder asks the height of the wall. Ms. Riemenschneider says it 
is eight (8) feet. Mr. Rieder echoes that it would be better to have something living 
in this space. 
Mr. Rieder appreciates that they are planting new trees on Margin Street. He 
doesn’t know how existing trees can stay alive when so much soil is to be removed. 
Think it is admirable to save the right hand side trees but to remove the two (2) in 
the middle. Ms. Riemenschneider says that she has chosen Prairie Pride hackberry as 
they are salt tolerant. Mr. Rieder says that they drop berries and feels elms or 
Swamp White oak would be better. Mr. Rieder says that the arborvitae could get 
enormous. He is happy with the progress on the Endicott Street corner but would 
like to get one more tree in there.  
Ms. Eimert asks when they expect the DRB recommendation. Mr. Connolly hopes to 
have that done with the DRB meeting on October 28, 2026. 
A motion to continue to the November 5, 2026, regular Planning Board meeting, is made by 
Sarah Tarbet, seconded by Graham Wing, and passes 9-0 in a roll call vote.

D. 57 Wharf Street Units UCB and UCC, and 201 Derby Street (Map 34, Lot 408)  
Applicant: Christina Granese f/b/o Pickering Wharf Complex, LLC; Rockett Manag & 
Realty CO 
Description: A continuation of public hearing for all persons interested in the 
application of Christina Granese f/b/o Pickering Wharf Complex, LLC; Rockett Manag 
& Realty CO at 57 Wharf Street Units UCB and UCC, and 201 Derby Street (Map 34, 
Lot 408) in the B5 Central Development Zoning District, Flood Hazard Overlay District 
(FHOD) and Coastal Resilience Overlay District (C-ROD) for Site Plan Review and C-
ROD Site Plan Review in accordance with sections 9.5 Site Plan Review and 8.9 Costal 
Resilience Overlay District of the Salem Zoning Ordinance. Specifically, the applicant 
proposes to demolish the second floor, third floor, attic, and roof of the existing 
building to accommodate 3 new floors with a total of 18 new dwelling units.   
 
Mr. Turiel recuses himself 7:05 pm.  
 
Attorney Grover, Michael Zmetrovich, Pickering Wharf complex management, 
Walter Jacob and Eli Albanese, Walter Jacob Architects are in attendance for the 
applicant.  
 
Mr. Jacob shares his screen. They have modified the renderings and included images 
to support the architectural style, including The Marblehead Boatyard Building on 
Front Street in Marblehead. The lighting and planting plans have been further 
developed.  
 
On signage, they realized that they could not have the large size signs. On plantings. 
There is an overhead wire. They are proposing two (2) street trees. Switch grass and 
inkberry as well. Along Wharf Street there are existing red maples, and they think it
City of Salem Planning Board 
Minutes October 15, 2026 
Page 6 of 15 
 
Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028 
through § 2-2033. 
will connect by adding another red maple and adding a combo of ground level 
juniper, inkberry and switch grass. On the roof, they will use switch grass and 
inkberry.  
 
On lighting, mostly City of Salem lights. Most of their lighting is recessed along the 
walkway to enter the building and at each store entrance there is a small, recessed 
light for safety. The alley between Wherry Row building and Derby Street buildings 
there is a light to light the passage. Everything is Dark Sky compliant. There are small 
lights, specific to each balcony. 
 
Public Comment 
 
None 
 
Planning Board Comments 
 
Ms. Tarbet on the architecture; likes the industrial look and the images to support 
the style. Struggling with the wrapping of the base. Allowing the volumes to 
complete at the ground would be better than floating up and reminiscing to the 
precedent buildings. And on the strip of the cladding, is an issue for her. Regarding 
the signage; she wonders if they even need signage. It is counter to what Mr. Jacob 
said about the lighting. Mr. Jacob will discuss with the client on what they are trying 
to achieve with their sign. Regarding the C-ROD requirement, curious if they thought 
about the landscape or site design in a way that would address future flooding?  Mr. 
Jacob will look at this, as well as the volumes.  Regarding C-ROD and accessibility, 
making it easy for people to get in the building also allows for water to get in. They 
are looking at ways to address the rising tides without disturbing the tenants; cannot 
raise the elevation without disruption. They will be renovating as there is a tenant 
turnover. Mechanical equipment, even for ground level units, will be moved above 
the flood elevation. 
 
Mr. Furey still does not care for the windows. 
 
Ms. Sides wonders how the corners are and there is a difference on the right side 
where the gables step back. Likely due to the building in the foreground. Wonders 
what it looks like from the other side.  
 
Ms. Eimert is curious about the material being used on the roof. Have they 
considered introducing white roof materials to the space? Particularly as it will be 
solar ready. Mr. Jacob thinks they could talk to the client about that, including 
lightening the decking.
City of Salem Planning Board 
Minutes October 15, 2026 
Page 7 of 15 
 
Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028 
through § 2-2033. 
Mr. Caunter likes that the project draws on historical inspiration. He is concerned 
that the proposed signage may be confusing, that people may think that the building 
itself is Pickering Wharf, particularly in October. Mr. Jacob understands about the 
signage and will discuss with the client.  
 
Mr. Rieder as an entity, the architecture is similar and this project starts to chip 
away at the monolith`. But so many residential buildings are being branded. But 
agrees with Mr. Jacob that the building should be the sign. Feels the new sign is an 
improvement, but that it is inelegant. Is distracted by the other signs that are on the 
building. Notes that the current yellow comes to the ground. Wonders if Ms. Tarbet 
would  want the blue to come down or the blue should not come down to the 
ground. Ms. Tarbet says that it could be successful either way. Ms. Sides says a 
simple solution is a corner board; it is hard to see at this angle. But doesn’t think the 
blue needs to go all the way down.  
 
Mr. Rieder would like them to consider Jefferson or Princeton Elm or Swamp White 
oak. There will be a deactivated fire pole box, and they could advocate to move one 
of the trees.  
 
Mr. Rieder asks if it is truly a ramp and how steep is it? Mr. Jacob says it is over five 
(5) percent. Mr. Rieder asks if there is a five (5) foot diameter to allow for 
accessibility? Mr. Jacob says that the whole project has been checked for 
accessibility. Mr. Rieder likes the industrial-type windows, bringing diversity to the 
site. 
A motion to continue to November 5, 2026, is made by Elena Eimert, seconded by Helen Sides, 
and passes 8-0 with one recusal in a roll call vote.

Description: A continuance of a public hearing for all persons interested in the 
application of 75 North Street LLC located at 75 North Street (Map 26, Lot 58), 3

the North River Canal Corridor (NRCC), Entrance Corridor Overlay District (ECOD), 
Flood Hazard Overlay District (FHOD), and Coastal Resilience Overlay District (C-ROD) 
for C-ROD Site Plan Review in accordance with Section 8.9 of the Salem Zoning 
Ordinance. Specifically, the applicant proposes to implement flood proofing 
measures in accordance with Section 8.9 of the Salem Zoning Ordinance to the 
previously approved multifamily residential building. City of Salem Planning Board 
Agenda for October 15, 2026.

F. 370 376 Highland Avenue (Map 3, Lot 63) 378 380 Highland Avenue (Map 3, Lot 
64), 382 Highland Avenue (Map 3, Lot 65)  
Applicant: Joseph Correnti f/b/o GR Development LLC  
Description: A public hearing for all persons interested in the application Joseph 
Correnti f/b/o GR Development LLC for the property located at 370 376 Highland 
Avenue (Map 3, Lot 63) 378 380 Highland Avenue (Map 3, Lot 64) and 382 Highland 
Avenue (Map 3, Lot 65) in the (B2) Business Highway and (ECOD) Entrance Corridor 
Overlay District zoning districts for Site Plan Review in accordance with Section 9.5 
of the Salem Zoning Ordinance. Specifically, the applicant proposes to demolish two 
existing buildings onsite, "Puleo's Dairy" and a storage facility, to construct a 4,400 
s.f. car wash facility. 24 onsite parking spaces are proposed, 22 of which will also be 
used as vacuum stations.  
 
Attorney Joseph Correnti, Bob Griffin, Griffin Engineering, Scott Thornton, Vanasse 
Associates, and Frank Dougherty, Washville are in attendance. 
 
Mr. Dougherty shares information on Washville. Twenty eight (28) facilities from 
Long Island to Maine with six (6) under construction in Massachusetts and New 
Hampshire. They have stealth vacuums and system enclosures which help to comply 
with city’s noise ordinance. There are full-time employees monitoring site and 
defined hours that respect the surrounding neighborhood.  
 
Mr. Griffin shares his screen. Currently there are three (3) entries off Highland 
Avenue as well as access off Savona Street. Will remove all buildings on site. Will put
City of Salem Planning Board 
Minutes October 15, 2026 
Page 10 of 15 
 
Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028 
through § 2-2033. 
in drainage system meeting stormwater system requirements and MassDEP 
requirements. Puleo’s sign is to be used for the Washville facility There are fourteen 
(14) or fifteen (15) foot grade changes on the site. There is a grade back to the top 
left of picture. Plan is to remove the three (3) Highland Avenue entrances and 
replace with one (1) twenty four (24) foot wide entrance on the side of the site 
abutting St. Jeans Credit Union. There will be plenty of area and frontage to meet 
Business Highway District (BHD) zoning. They do not need any zoning relief. The flow 
of traffic through the site allows for exiting to Savona Street or Highland Avenue or 
turning to use the self-service vacuums. There are twenty four (24) parking spaces, 
with twenty two (22) having access to vacuum hoses. The remaining two (2) are for 
the full time staff. The spaces are bigger than required. Site plan shows box off 
Northwest end of building; this is where vacuum canister will be installed. There are 
four (4) tanks under the pavement where the wash water treatment is stored, and 
they can recycle as much as practical. On Ravenna  Avenue and Highland Avenue 
intersection, the stormwater management/drainage system will be placed and go to 
an underground filtration system. There will be an overflow connecting to the drains 
on Highland Avenue that will require Mass Highway approval. All utilities necessary 
to run the facility are on the existing site; the team will modify the connections to 
meet Washville’s requirements. Dumpster enclosure is at the back of the property 
along Savona Street. There will be significant wayfinding on Savona Street to move 
traffic back to Highland Avenue. Post/rail fence proposed between Washville and St. 
Jeans property. The team expects the project to go to the Design Review Board 
(DRB) due to location in the ECOD and the size of the facility. Propose to save an 
existing hedge on Ravenna Avenue as well install a concrete wall with fence to 
provide some screening. Lighting is proposed to be dark sky compliant, shoebox 
style with parking lot lights pointing downward. There will be soffit lights on the 
building. Photometrics are nearly zero (0) at the lot lines and there are lumens 
throughout the site’s walking areas. Landscaping along Highland Avenue will be one 
hundred and sixty (160) feet of Japanese Yews. Along/near Ravenna Avenue there 
are a total of fifteen (15) deciduous trees, eight (8) arborvitaes, and a number of 
pine trees. There will be shrubs and perennials in the planting beds. Metal roof and 
stone along the base of the building with cementitious siding. 
 
Mr. Thornton says that a full traffic study has been prepared but will do a deep dive 
in the future. Expecting to work with the city’s Department of Transportation and 
the peer reviewer. The project is a minor traffic generator. Having access out to 
Savona Street is preferred design. With wayfinding sign, it will encourage traffic back 
to Highland Avenue. Increases are one to two (1-2) trips per minute during peak 
hours. With a one and a half  to three (1 ½ -3 %) percent increase in peak hours.  
 
Mr. Correnti says they had a productive one stop meeting. They have also worked 
with Councilor Flynn to have a neighborhood meeting.
City of Salem Planning Board 
Minutes October 15, 2026 
Page 11 of 15 
 
Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028 
through § 2-2033. 
 
Public Comment  
 
Written Public Comment 
 
Councilor Tim Flynn 
42 Sable Road 
Ward 4 Councilor 
Glad the team had a neighborhood meeting. Is still concerned with the use of 
Savona Street and this use is one of the major issue the neighbors have. There is also 
the consideration of the new gas station opening on the corner of Barcelona Avenue 
and Highland Avenue; the two sites have the potential to have drivers go through 
the neighborhood from one site to the other. An increase in traffic like this would be 
problematic. Also, vehicles leaving Savonna Street, take a look and contact Mass 
DOT, it could affect the traffic flow out of the car wash. 
 
Helen Hughes 
24 Ravenna Avenue 
Agrees with Councilor Flynn. Even now with the gas station, traffic is increasing. 
There are a number of children in the neighborhood. Is there a way that the car 
wash could use St. Jean’s pathways to exit? On the pumping station, can the water 
station handle it? Feels this will create traffic jams.  
 
Planning Board Comments 
 
Mr. Furey remembers when Mr. Puleo wanted to put in a mini golf course and the 
neighbors said no. Salem already has two (2) car washes; can a third survive?  
 
Mr. Berk recalls the Popeye’s project and the concerns with traffic filtering into the 
surrounding neighborhood. It would be worse here as there is no outlet from the 
side streets. Doesn’t see reason for why they need a second egress.   
 
Ms. Eimert would like to hear the necessity of using Savona Street. Regarding the 
public comment on water usage, the Engineering peer review will catch any issues. 
Her question for the team is… is there any ability to reduce the amount of parking in 
the lot? She notes that they should contact the Department of Transportation (DOT) 
on the reconfiguration project as they may affect the site layout. Mr. Dougherty says 
the spaces outside the carwash are primarily for the vacuums and there are two (2) 
employee parking spots; the rest are vacuum spaces.  
 
Ms. Sides seconds concerns with amount of asphalt.
City of Salem Planning Board 
Minutes October 15, 2026 
Page 12 of 15 
 
Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028 
through § 2-2033. 
Mr. Rieder also questions two way in and out on Highland Avenue and Savona Street 
but could have one-way in on Savona Street and 2 way out on Highland. The credit 
union is a different owner, but the applicant wants a sign on the property? 
Additionally, Mr. Griffin said “rehabilitate” the sign, but the renderings show a sign 
significantly larger. Mr. Correnti says that any permissions will be in place regarding 
this. Mr. Rieder thinks the project should refer to the DRB. Didn’t see vertical granite 
curbing? Mr. Griffin says they are in the detail sheets. The Entrance Corridor Overlay 
District (ECOD) says three (3) trees for every parking space. He invites the team to 
reassess to add more shade trees on an active corridor. Feels that too many of the 
plantings are not native. Thinks the planting plan is not keeping up with more 
current planting plans.
